bodyHtml:
An AI-powered bot that reviews merge requests and auto-approves when changes pass checks.

Uses an AI model to analyze merge request diffs for code quality and risk, then calls the GitLab API to approve automatically once the requested changes are verified.

  • Fetches MR diffs and comments through the GitLab API
  • Uses an AI model to review code changes against defined review criteria
  • Automatically re-checks requested changes and approves the MR once satisfied
  • Stack: Python, GitLab API, AI/LLM review model

Internal platform for validating and scoring large-scale datasets before release.

Built pipelines that automatically flag anomalies, missing fields, and schema drift across incoming data batches, cutting manual review time significantly.

  • Stack: Python, PostgreSQL, Kubernetes,, Kafka, GCP
  • Impact: reduced manual QA effort for 10+ downstream teams

bodyHtml:
Associated with Mercedes-Benz Research and Development India (Apr 2023 – Jan 2025).

Built automated analysis of head unit camera video feeds to validate and improve parking assistance functions, reducing manual review effort for parking system testing.

  • Automated video-based validation of parking camera feeds from the vehicle head unit
  • Supported engineering teams in verifying parking function behavior at scale
  • Stack: Computer Vision, Python, Automotive Head Unit Systems

bodyHtml:
Associated with Indian Institute of Space Science and Technology (Feb 2021 – Jun 2021).

Solved a state-of-the-art problem in Natural Language Processing using ML algorithms and published a relevant Python package yielding better results compared to the NLTK WSD function.

  • Tackled Word Sense Disambiguation, a core NLP challenge, using machine learning algorithms
  • Published a Python package that outperformed NLTK's built-in WSD function
  • Stack: Python, NLTK, Machine Learning, NLP

title: OFDM Transceiver Using Software Defined Radio
description: Associated with K.K. Wagh Institute of Engineering Education & Research Sep 2017 – Mar 2018. Contributors: Pranali and Ruchira. Created an OFDM transceiver flow…
bodyHtml:
Associated with K.K. Wagh Institute of Engineering Education & Research (Sep 2017 – Mar 2018). Contributors: Pranali and Ruchira.

Created an OFDM transceiver flow graph covering different modulation schemes on an FPGA-based SDR kit, achieving large bandwidth coverage with different antennas to receive FM radio signals and transmit audio.

  • Implemented modulation schemes: ASK, BPSK, QPSK, QAM-16, QAM-256
  • Built the transceiver flow graph on an FPGA-based Software Defined Radio kit
  • Used different antennas to receive FM radio signals and transmit audio over large bandwidth
